tagline.text: Where a morning rainbow rises over a white curtain of forest water

location.label: Location
location.text: Burboanan, Bislig City, Surigao del Sur

items.credit: Bro. Jeffrey Pioquinto, SJ / CC BY 2.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: A broad, multi-tiered curtain waterfall about
high and

wide, known as the Niagara of the Philippines. You can ride a bamboo raft right up to the base of the cascading water, and on clear mornings a rainbow rises over the spray — a signature attraction of Surigao del Sur.
Tinuy-an Falls is a waterfall in the tropical forest of Burboanan village, Bislig City, on Mindanao's east coast in Surigao del Sur Province. At about
high, it isn't especially tall, but its width of about

makes the whole river cascade down like a broad white curtain. The falls drop in several tiers, with water from the upper tier flowing over wide rock steps down to the next, and the largest, widest bottom tier is its signature view. This appearance is why Filipinos call it the "Niagara of the Philippines."

The falls take their name from the Cebuano word "tinuyoan," meaning "done on purpose." The legend behind the name is that the people of Mount Magdiwata, once enslaved by a tribe from Agusan, pushed a bamboo raft (gakit) toward the falls and sent their masters over the edge, winning back their freedom. The area around the falls belongs to the lush forest zone of Bislig, once famous for its timber industry, and is now protected as an ecotourism site managed jointly by the Bislig City tourism office and the Manobo tribal council. Below the falls the river forms a wide, shallow pool before flowing back into the forest, so you can both swim and ride a raft.
Tinuy-an Falls' signature feature is its morning rainbow. On clear days around

, sunlight hitting the falls' spray creates a vivid rainbow in front of the waterfall. Photos capturing the massive water curtain, the rainbow, and people on bamboo rafts all in one frame are a constant fixture of Surigao del Sur's tourism promotion.

The path from the entrance to the viewpoint and the water's edge is a maintained stairway, so children and seniors can go without strain. Together with the nearby Enchanted River and the Britania Islands, it forms the core of an east-coast Surigao del Sur trip, and is especially recommended for family travelers and those who love waterfalls and nature photography.

blocks.title: Riding a bamboo raft to the base of the falls

children.text: A local boatman poles a bamboo raft right up to the cascading water. Spray showers your whole body, so put electronics in a waterproof bag before boarding.
On clear days around
, a rainbow arcs in front of the falls. The viewing deck facing the falls and the rocks by the water's edge are the best spots to capture both the rainbow and the falls together.
The broad pool beneath the falls is shallow near the edges, good for swimming with a life vest on. The water is cold and clear, especially refreshing on a hot day.
Following the stairway path upward brings you close to the second and third tiers. With fewer people than the bottom tier, you can enjoy the sound of the water quietly.
Sitting on a rock beneath a shallow-tier cascade lets the falling water pound your shoulders like a natural massage. Only do this where your guide or the caretaker permits.
In front of the falls there are rental huts and tables where you can eat lunch while looking at the falls. This is the way local families enjoy it most.
Around the forest path from the entrance to the falls there are many kinds of birds and butterflies. In

, American birder Peter Kaestner became the first person in the world to record a 10,000th bird species, an Orange-tufted spiderhunter, in a heliconia thicket here. If you arrive early in the morning, you can hear the sounds of the forest more clearly.

Morning at Tinuy-an Falls (rainbow hours) → lunch → afternoon swim at Enchanted River (about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
away) → overnight in Hinatuan or Bislig. The fish feeding at Enchanted River has shifted between noon and 3 PM, so if it is at noon that day, swap the order and visit Enchanted River first.
Bislig Airport currently has no scheduled commercial flights, so use Davao Airport (DVO) or Butuan Airport (BXU). It's about
2 hours
from Manila to Davao and about
1 hour 40 minutes
to Butuan, with Davao having far more flights.
From Davao's Ecoland bus terminal, a Bislig (Mangagoy)-bound bus passes through Davao del Norte and Davao de Oro to reach downtown Bislig in about
5–6 hours
, for a fare of about
. From Butuan, buses and vans also run to Bislig/Mangagoy, taking about
5 hours
for about
. Take an air-conditioned bus departing in the morning so you arrive before dark.
From downtown Bislig (Mangagoy) to the falls is about
20km
. Chartering a habal-habal costs about
round trip (including waiting), while a vehicle with driver runs about

for half a day. By public transport, you can take a jeepney or multicab bound for Burboanan and get off at the village turnoff, then switch to a habal-habal, but service is infrequent, so if you're short on time, chartering is easier. To cover both this and Enchanted River in a day, renting a habal-habal or vehicle for the whole day is more efficient.
Surigao del Sur is one of the rainiest provinces in the Philippines; from
November
to
February

, the northeast monsoon brings rain nearly every day. During this period, the falls carry much more water and look grand, but the water turns muddy, and rafting and swimming are sometimes suspended for safety.
The relatively dry period from
March
to
September

is the best time to visit. Clear water and clearing skies are more common, raising your chances of seeing the morning rainbow. However, if the dry season runs long, water volume can drop and the curtain may thin out somewhat. Weekends, holidays, and the April–
May
summer break bring crowds of local tourists, so arriving early on a weekday morning is best.

Staying in downtown Bislig, especially the commercial area of Mangagoy, is the most convenient option. There are business hotels and pensions at about

per night, close to restaurants, ATMs, and the bus terminal for easy transport. Small lodgings sometimes operate near the falls too, but facilities are basic and availability changes, so check in advance. If also visiting Enchanted River, Hinatuan's coastal resorts are an alternative.

The falls' entrance has stalls selling simple food and drinks, but it's better to buy grilled chicken (litson manok), fish, rice, and fruit at the market like a local and eat it at a cottage. As a coastal city, Bislig lets you enjoy cheap seafood like crab, shrimp, and shellfish from the Mangagoy market and beach eateries, with coconut-milk ginataan stew and vinegar-cured kinilaw common dishes.
To see the morning rainbow, arrive before
9 AM
and pick a clear day. On overcast days, the rainbow rarely appears.
Downtown Bislig has ATMs, but the falls area is cash only, so bring small bills for the entrance fee, raft, and cottage costs.
Riding the raft soaks you completely, so wear a rash guard over your swimsuit and hang your phone from your neck in a waterproof pouch.
The rocks in front of the falls are very slippery with moss, so wear aqua shoes or strap sandals.
A wide-angle lens lets you capture the whole broad waterfall in one frame, and a tripod enables long-exposure shots that render the water smoothly.
Weekend afternoons get crowded with families, so weekday mornings are recommended.
Cell signal is weak, so arrange a return time with your habal-habal driver in advance.

After heavy rain, the falls' water volume surges sharply and the current becomes very strong. Always follow the caretaker if they suspend swimming or rafting, and never enter the flow directly beneath the falls.
Wearing a life vest is mandatory when swimming, and you must not cross the marked boundary into deep or fast-moving areas.
The falls and forest are a protected area, so take your trash with you and don't use soap or shampoo or collect plants and animals.
The entrance fee, operating hours, and activity fees can change under Bislig city regulations, so check the latest notices before visiting.
During the rainy season, landslides and flooding can occur on roads, so allow extra time for long-distance bus schedules.
Some parts of Mindanao carry travel advisories, so check your foreign ministry's travel safety information before departing and avoid night-time long-distance travel.
